paragraphs: Apple might add touchscreens to all its high-end MacBook Pros next year, leaving only the entry-level 14-inch model with a traditional display.
The rumor that Apple will make touch standard on every MacBook Pro with a Pro or Max chip comes just days after the company unveiled its first touchscreen MacBook Pro.

Apple claimed for years that adding a touchscreen to a Mac would be some sort of abomination. But that went out the window last Wednesday when the company unveiled the awkwardly named MacBook Pro with PROLED XDR Display.

The first touchscreen Mac comes with a lighter, thinner design and either M5 Pro or M5 Max processors inside. However, Apple left non-touchscreen versions of the MacBook Pro with those same processors, introduced earlier this year, in its expanded product lineup.

Bloomberg’s Mark Gurman reported on the plan to slim down MacBook Pro options in his Power On newsletter Sunday. He predicted Apple will phase out the non-touch M5 Pro and M5 Max models when second-generation touch MacBooks arrive in 2027. Gurman previously said those second-generation models will run on M7 Pro and M7 Max chips with advanced AI capabilities.

The entry-level 14-inch MacBook Pro is said to be the exception. It will move to the base M7 chip and adopt the thinner, lighter design with slimmer bezels, but won’t add a touchscreen. That model currently runs an M6 chip and starts at $1,999.
The new touchscreen MacBook Pros come with a tandem OLED display. Apple also replaced the screen notch with a Dynamic Island (although the laptops lack Face ID).
The 14-inch touchscreen model with M5 Pro chip starts at $2,899, while the 16-inch version starts at $3,399. The touchscreen configurations cost $400 more than the matching non-touch models.
